## 裁决 — triage's grade, and its serial precondition is DISCHARGED

Triage seat, 2026-08-24: `domain:ui` + `pm:queue`, Task. Verbatim: *"last instance of the #5113 class, inherits that card's judgment (catalog entries author the component their package registers, not hand-built look-alikes). Serial: verify #5113's PR is merged first; reuse its shape."*

**I verified it: #5113 is CLOSED, via PR #5857 (`docs(plugin-view): make the three "Interactive Examples" real object-view nodes`), state MERGED.** The precondition is satisfied and the fence is spent. ✅ Reuse #5857's shape — read that PR before writing anything; it is the worked example of this exact fix one category over.

**The inherited judgment, stated so you do not have to re-derive it:** a catalog entry mounted under a `PluginLoader` for a given plugin must **author a type that plugin registers**. `plugin-grid`'s two entries (`product-inventory-grid`, `team-members-grid`) author only `badge button card flex stack text` — pictures of a grid, not a grid. Every other `plugin-*` category already authors its own type (`calendar-view`, `chart`/`bar-chart`, `chatbot`, `dashboard`, `code-editor`, `object-gantt`, `kanban`, `object-map`, `markdown`, `timeline`, `form`, and since #5113, `object-view`). `plugin-grid` is the last one left.

## ⛔ The trap that will cost you the round if you miss it

**Deleting a catalog entry moves three corpus-wide counters:** `NODE_CENSUS` in `layout-dom-leak-5574.test.tsx`, and two floors in `layout-props-conversion.test.tsx` (the `className`-carrying layout node count, and the `stack` node count).

⛔ **Do not "fix" this by deleting the two mock-ups.** #5113 **re-seated** its three mock-ups into honest categories precisely so no floor had to move, and that is the shape to reuse. If your change moves any of those three counters, ⛔ **stop and report** rather than editing a floor — a floor that moves because a fixture was deleted is indistinguishable, six months later, from a floor that moved because coverage regressed. If re-seating genuinely cannot preserve them, say why and what the exact deltas are.

## Scope

1. **Author real `object-grid` entries** for the `plugin-grid` category, the way #5857 authored real `object-view` ones.
2. **Re-seat whatever of the two mock-ups is worth keeping** into an honest category (they are legitimate static layouts — they are just filed under the wrong plugin). Preserve the three counters.
3. **Extend #5113's pin to `plugin-grid`.** #5857 added `objectui#5113 — the plugin-view entries render THROUGH object-view` in `examples/schema-catalog/test/catalog-gallery-render.test.tsx`, asserting that every entry in the category authors an `object-view` node **and** that the rendered tile shows a record existing only in the gallery's data source. ✅ The second half is what makes it a real pin rather than a grep — reuse both halves.
4. ⛔ **Do NOT generalize the pin to all of `plugin-*`.** #5113 deliberately left it per-category because the general rule needs a per-plugin map of which types each package registers — and **`plugin-grid` was the specific reason it could not simply be turned on.** Once this card lands that blocker is gone, which makes generalizing a **follow-up card, not this one**. ✅ File it as a finding (unassigned, no labels — triage grades it) and say in it that this card removed its last obstacle.

## PM mechanism assumptions — measure, do not assume

1. **The card asserts the machinery already exists after #5113: `object-grid` reaches data the same way `object-view` does — `dataSource` is a prop the registered renderer pulls off `SchemaRendererContext`, not a schema key — and #5113 gave `apps/site/app/components/galleryDataSource.ts` the object surface (`getObjectSchema` / `find` / `findOne` / writes) with `InteractiveDemo` pointed at it.** ⛔ Do not assume that transfers cleanly. **Verify on your merge-base** that a real `object-grid` node actually renders against that fixture — if `ObjectGrid` needs something `ObjectView` did not (a column source, an object schema shape, a different context key), that is the whole difficulty of this card and it must be measured before you author two entries against a hope.
2. **The type-set reading is from the #5113 *branch*, not from `main`.** Re-run the walk on your own merge-base and report the current type sets for both entries. The card's own re-check recipe is in #5113 and is reusable.
3. ⚠️ **The two existing gates cannot see this defect, by construction** — `check-doc-component-types` only asks whether each `type` is registered (`card`/`flex`/`badge` all are), and `catalog-gallery-render.test.tsx` only asks whether the tile draws (these do). So ⛔ **a green gate run is not evidence your fix worked.** The new pin is the only thing that can tell the difference, which is why item 3 is not optional.
4. **`content/docs/plugins/plugin-grid.mdx` mounts these under a `PluginLoader` for a plugin they do not use.** Check whether the page's own prose claims these are the plugin's output; if it does, the prose moves with the entries. ⛔ But stay out of `content/docs/releases/**` entirely (CLAUDE.md).

## Verification

Reverse-verify with the direction predicted **before** running: revert one entry to a hand-built layout and show the new pin goes **red**; prove the mutation on disk by grepping the injected text **and separately** the removed text (an editor's exit code proves nothing on a zero-hit anchor); restore under `trap … EXIT INT TERM` and confirm `git diff HEAD --stat` is empty afterwards.

**Counter-probe required, both halves of the pin:** (a) an entry that authors `object-grid` but renders **no** gallery-only record must fail the data half — otherwise the pin passes on a grid wired to nothing; (b) the `plugin-view` entries #5857 landed must stay green under your generalisation of the pin, proving you extended it rather than replaced it.

Gates by name with exit codes: root-form vitest over `examples/schema-catalog` **and** the two counter-carrying suites `layout-dom-leak-5574.test.tsx` / `layout-props-conversion.test.tsx` (⚠️ this repo's vitest guard refuses the `--filter` forms — use `pnpm exec vitest run <paths>` from the repo root), plus `node scripts/check-doc-component-types.mjs`, `node scripts/check-doc-snippet-types.mjs` and `node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs`, each quoting its **own** verdict line rather than `$?` after a pipe.

Run `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` rather than guessing whether a changeset is owed; empty frontmatter is this repo's "releases nothing" declaration. Draft PR, `Fixes #5856`. Post the terminal report here (plain-text first-line marker `os-dev-report`; ⛔ avoid short angle-bracket placeholders in prose — this repo's sanitizer eats them) and return it.

## PM review — **ACCEPT**

PR #6028, head `8d0a3502e`, merge-base `d2fb6efb4`. Gate read at the usual mark.

### The counter trap — cleared, and git certifies it

This was the one thing that could have cost the round, so I checked it directly rather than reading your counter table:

```
R100  examples/schema-catalog/src/schemas/plugin-grid/product-inventory-grid.json
   -> examples/schema-catalog/src/schemas/components-layout-card/inventory-table-card.json
R100  examples/schema-catalog/src/schemas/plugin-grid/team-members-grid.json
   -> examples/schema-catalog/src/schemas/components-layout-card/team-roster-card.json
```

**`R100` — pure renames at 100% similarity, zero content change.** Git itself certifies the mock-ups are byte-identical, so every node they contain is preserved and all three corpus counters are invariant *by construction*, not by measurement agreeing afterwards. ✅ That is stronger evidence than the before/after numbers, and the numbers corroborate it (`flex/stack/container/grid/text` 248/153/15/26/699 identical; `className`-carrying layout nodes 178 → 178; stack nodes 153 → 153).

And the two counter-carrying suites are **untouched** — `git diff` against `layout-dom-leak-5574` and `layout-props-conversion` returns nothing. ⛔ No floor edited, which was the non-negotiable.

✅ **`NODE_CENSUS` is asserted with `toEqual`, not as a floor — so that suite going green IS the proof it did not move.** Naming *why* the green is evidence, rather than just reporting a green, is the distinction this lane keeps asking for.

### PM assumption 3, confirmed empirically rather than argued

I told you a green gate run is not evidence your fix worked, because neither existing gate can see this defect by construction. You did not take that on faith — you **measured it**: on the reverted entry, the pre-existing objectui#4616 sweep reported *"plugin-grid/object-grid-columns renders without a red tile"* **GREEN**. So the old gates demonstrably cannot see it, and the new pin is demonstrably the only thing that can. ✅ Turning an assumption I handed you into a reading is worth more than obeying it.

### The pin

✅ Both halves kept, and the structure/data split is real: reverting `object-grid-columns` to the hand-built layout turned **both** red (`authors a object-grid node`, `puts data from the gallery data source on screen`), and counter-probe (a) — an entry authoring `object-grid` but wired to the inline `value` provider — turned **only the data half** red. That is the probe that stops the pin passing on a grid wired to nothing, and it discriminates. Counter-probe (b): all three of #5857's `plugin-view` entries still pass, so the pin was **extended, not replaced**.

✅ **And `CATEGORY_OWN_TYPE` is enumerated with a written prohibition against the wrong generalisation:**

> what a reader must **NOT** do is convert this into a loop over every `plugin-*` category with an exemption list, which would turn each remaining gap into a silent entry in a table rather than a card someone owns.

That sentence is the reason #5113 scoped its pin in the first place, now written where the next person will hit it. ✅ And asserting registration **first, separately from the render**, is the right structure given #6025.

### PM assumption 1 — measured, and the answer was the good one

I said the transfer of #5113's machinery was the whole difficulty of this card and must not be assumed. You measured it: `object-grid` renders against `galleryDataSource` with **nothing `ObjectView` did not need** — no column source, no different object-schema shape, no other context key — and a bare `object-grid` with no columns at all resolves headers from `getObjectSchema` and paints select option labels and formatted dates. ✅ Reporting *what you checked for and did not find* is what makes that a measurement rather than a shrug.

### #6025 is the find

> the gallery's registration of `object-grid` is **TRANSITIVE** — `HOST_PACKAGES` / `registerCatalogBlocks.ts` never name `@object-ui/plugin-grid`, and the type only arrives because `@object-ui/plugin-view` imports `ObjectGrid` from it.

The card did not anticipate this and neither did my dispatch. ✅ It is latent rather than broken *today*, and the failure mode is precisely the kind this repo keeps getting bitten by: the new entries render, every gate is green, and the thing holding them up is an import in a **different package** that nobody has declared they depend on. If `plugin-view` ever stops importing `ObjectGrid`, this category goes dark and the pin you just wrote is what turns red — which is the good outcome, and worth saying out loud. ✅ Correctly filed rather than fixed: `apps/site/**` was outside your declared surface.

✅ **#6024** is filed with what still has to be *decided* rather than just "generalize it" — `plugin-charts` authors two types so the map value must become a set, and the RENDER half does not transfer to categories that are not object-bound, with `plugin-editor` / `plugin-map` additionally unrenderable in that suite. A follow-up card that already names its own obstacles is one someone can pick up cold.

### Two smaller things, both right

- ✅ **`check-doc-snippet-types` first EXIT=1 with `[unbuilt-package]` for 20 packages was read as a fresh-worktree precondition, not a finding** — built under the shared verify lock (waited 178 s, held 310 s: correct behaviour on a contended lock with four sibling cards live) and re-run to `148 of 148 block(s) judged, 0 failed`.
- ✅ **The changeset was added even though `check-changeset-presence` said none was owed** (*"No source of a released package changed in this range"*). Empty frontmatter is this repo's explicit "releases nothing" declaration, and declaring nothing beats declaring by omission. You ran the script instead of guessing in either direction — which is the rule — and then made the more legible choice.
